title: How to Do Calf Raises for Beginners (Calf Exercise at Home)
intro: The calf raise is a tiptoe up-and-down exercise to strengthen your calves and ankles. It's very simple and you can do it while brushing your teeth, waiting for water to boil or during a break at the office.
muscles: Calf muscles (gastrocnemius and soleus), muscles around the ankle and sole of the foot. It helps with stability when walking and climbing stairs. Calf raises don't burn calf fat specifically; fat reduces from the whole body.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, hold a wall or chair if needed.
Push through the balls of your feet and lift your heels as high as you can.
Lower your heels slowly over 2-3 seconds.
mistakes: Bouncing up and down fast. Move slowly so your calf muscles really work.
Weight falling onto the outer toes or ankles rolling to the side. Press through your big toe and second toe.
Only going halfway up. Lift your heels as high as is comfortable.
easier: Do it seated on a chair with your hands pressing lightly on your knees, or standing while holding firmly onto a wall.
harder: Do one leg at a time, or stand on the edge of a stair step so your heels can drop lower.
dose: Beginner: 2-3 sets x 12-15 reps, rest 30-60 seconds. Can do 3-5 times a week.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your heel, Achilles tendon or ankle. If you have long-lasting heel pain, an ankle injury or swelling in your calf, see a doctor or physiotherapist.

faq.q: Can calf raises make my calves smaller?
faq.a: Calf raises strengthen your calf muscles, they don't burn fat there. Calf size is largely influenced by genetics and overall body fat. Focus on eating sensible portions and daily movement.

faq.q: Can I do them while brushing my teeth or waiting for the lift?
faq.a: Yes, this is the easiest way to sneak exercise into a busy day. 15 reps while brushing your teeth morning and night already counts as good.

faq.q: Why do my calves cramp when I do them?
faq.a: Maybe your muscles aren't used to it yet, or you haven't drunk enough water. Rest, stretch your calves gently and drink water. Reduce the reps next session and build up bit by bit.
